Gemini 4 on Antigravity, Gemini and Vertex, Google's prices, T3 Code 0.1.11's pricing rules, and two fixes for stale account status.

## Changes

- **Gemini 4 Neon, Carbon and Hydrogen are built-in models.**
  - Antigravity: `gemini-4-neon-{xhigh,high,medium,low}`, `gemini-4-carbon-{high,medium,low}` and `gemini-4-hydrogen-{xhigh,high,medium,low}`. A bare name such as `gemini-4-neon` goes to `-high`, Antigravity's default.
  - Gemini (AI Studio) and Vertex: `gemini-4-neon`, `gemini-4-carbon` and `gemini-4-hydrogen`.
  - With a Gemini API key and an Antigravity account, a bare `gemini-4-neon` used to become `gemini-4-neon-high` and go to the Gemini key, which has no such model. The Gemini key now gets the bare name, and `-high` names stay on Antigravity.
- **`xhigh` thinking on Gemini 4 Neon and Hydrogen.** `xhigh` and `max` used to become `high` on every Gemini model. They now become `xhigh` on Neon and Hydrogen, on all three providers. Other models keep `high`.
- **Antigravity's Claude 4.6 and GPT-OSS models are no longer offered.** Google removes them on 30 November 2026. An Antigravity account whose own list still reports them serves them until then. Claude and Codex accounts never take `claude-opus-4-6-thinking` or `gpt-oss-120b-medium`.
- **Antigravity identity 2.33.0.** The user agent now has the language server's form, with the release's build number (`antigravity/hub/2.33.0 (aidev_client; os_type=darwin; arch=arm64; cl=1023160026)`). When Google ships a newer release, Fusebox reads its build number from the release itself (about 37 MB of range requests, nothing saved), and until then keeps claiming the newest release it has a number for. `scripts/antigravity-build.py` prints a release's number.
- **Google's prices.** Gemini, Vertex and Antigravity requests were not priced before. Rate card `2026-11-20.1` and default catalogue `t3-2026-11-20.2` add Google's list prices (per million tokens):

  | Model | Input | Cached input | Output |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Gemini 4 Neon | $3.00 | $0.15 | $15.00 |
  | Gemini 4 Hydrogen | $1.50 | $0.075 | $7.50 |
  | Gemini 4 Carbon, Argon (from 1 Dec 2026) | $2.00 ($4.00) | $0.10 ($0.20) | $10.00 ($20.00) |
  | Gemini 3.8, 3.7, 3.6 Flash (from 1 Jan 2027) | $0.75 ($1.50) | $0.075 ($0.15) | $3.75 ($7.50) |
  | Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite | $0.30 | $0.03 | $2.50 |
  | Gemini 3.1 Pro (prompt above 200K) | $2.00 ($4.00) | $0.20 ($0.40) | $12.00 ($18.00) |

  - Fusebox switches to the announced December and January prices by itself on those dates.
  - Antigravity requests drop the effort from the name and use the maker's price (`gemini-4-neon-xhigh` → `gemini-4-neon`, `claude-opus-5-5-max` → `claude-opus-5-5`). Claude on Antigravity reports no cache writes, so its price is a labelled estimate.
  - The dashboard's account test now uses `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` on Gemini, Vertex and Antigravity accounts, the cheapest priced model.
- **Prices follow T3 Code 0.1.11.** The default calculation now prices two things it did not:
  - **Long prompts.** When a request's whole prompt (uncached input, cache reads and writes) is above a model's threshold, every category uses the long-prompt rate: GPT-5.4 and newer above 272K, Claude Haiku 5.5 above 100K, Muse Ember above 200K.
  - **One-hour Claude cache writes** cost twice the input rate; five-minute writes stay at 1.25 times.
  - Catalogue `t3-2026-11-20.1` (then `.2` with Google's models) is compiled from LiteLLM. The rates themselves did not change. Over the last 30 days of our own traffic, the new rules add about $1 to $3 to roughly $43,000 of estimates.
- **A passing refresh error clears itself.** A 503 from a token endpoint left "refresh failed" on the account until a request through it succeeded, so an idle account showed it for days. It now ends when a refresh works or the account signs in again.
- **The quota bar shows a banked reset.** Right after a reset, the usage endpoint can still return the old numbers, and the bar stayed full for 5 to 30 minutes. Fusebox now reads again a few times in the next 20 seconds, then every minute for 5 minutes, until the reset shows.

## Upgrading

- **Database.** No change; the usage database stays on schema 5.
- **No new settings** and no API changes.
- **Prices.** Gemini, Vertex and Antigravity requests that were unpriced only for lack of a rate are priced at the next start. Estimates already saved keep their price until you run `fusebox usage reprice --all`.

Details: [Gemini 4 and Antigravity](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.18.0/docs/model-support-2026-11-20.md) and [T3 Code 0.1.11 pricing](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.18.0/docs/usage-pricing-t3-2026-11-20.md).

Validation: the Rust, dashboard and Python test suites passed, and formatting and Clippy passed; the Release workflow tests the tag on Linux, macOS and Windows. Running in production since 20 November 2026. No Antigravity, Gemini or Vertex account was used for the model changes; they are checked against Google's documents and the published Antigravity app.

[Full comparison with v0.17.3](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/compare/v0.17.3...v0.18.0).
